title: Computability reduction from halting to the diagonal function
statement: Let $c$ be an effective machine representation scheme, and suppose the function that maps each bit string $s$ to the one-bit string whose bit is the halting value of $c$ on $s$ is computable. Then the function mapping each bit string $\alpha$ to the one-bit string whose bit is the diagonal value of $c$ at $\alpha$ is computable.
hypotheses_covered: the one-bit halting function for $c$ is computable
replaced:
Let $c$ be an effective coding scheme for Turing machines, i.e.\ one admitting a
universal evaluator machine. Write $\mathrm{HALT}_c$ for the halting function of
$c$: it is true on a bit string $s$ exactly when $s$ is the pairing encoding
$\langle \alpha, x \rangle$ of two bit strings and the machine denoted by $\alpha$
under $c$ halts on input $x$, and false otherwise. Write $\mathrm{UC}_c$ for the
diagonal function that maps a bit string $\alpha$ to false when the machine
denoted by $\alpha$ under $c$ outputs the single bit true on input $\alpha$
within some finite number of steps, and to true otherwise. If the function
mapping $s$ to the one-bit string carrying $\mathrm{HALT}_c(s)$ is computable by
a Turing machine, then so is the function mapping $\alpha$ to the one-bit string
carrying $\mathrm{UC}_c(\alpha)$ [AB09, proof of Theorem 1.11].
